title: Space A Hub — C2: Read-only REST Contract
description: Read-only endpoints consumed by Pillar 3 (community visualization). v2 is aligned with Pillar 3's actual data contract (docs/design/frontend-viz/03-architecture.md §4): Space is a first-class entity, ReuseEvent is a first-class event, issues carry a transition timeline, and narrative text is OFFERED (not imposed) as a server-side option. Pillar 3 does NOT connect to the graph DB directly: doing so would turn the graph schema into a public API and freeze it. The only write path into Space A is C1 (MCP).

consumerAutonomy.description: WHAT THIS CONTRACT DOES NOT DECIDE. Pillar 3 owns the visualization service; this contract supplies data and must not dictate how that service is built. Earlier drafts overstepped here — they said the frontend 'must NOT assemble' narrative text, which silently closed Pillar 3's own open question Q4 (narrative-translation pipeline: agent-at-write vs backend batch vs view server). That is Pillar 3's call, not this contract's.
pillar3Decides: Whether a visualization agent generates the human-facing narrative, or it is rendered deterministically from structured fields, or the server's precomputed text is used as-is. Any mix is fine; different surfaces may choose differently.
Which scenarios warrant an LLM in the loop and which need deterministic output.
thisContractGuarantees: STRUCTURED fields are always present (ids, types, timestamps, counts, statuses) — so a consumer can always build its own narrative, or feed an agent, without parsing prose.
NARRATIVE fields (summary, status_line, highlight, chain[].label, node label) are OFFERED ready-made — so a consumer that wants none of that work can just render them.
Both are available on every call. The consumer picks; the server does not care which.
nonNegotiable: Tier trimming. WHO may see WHAT is enforced server-side and is not a rendering choice — see permissionModel. Whoever writes a guest-tier sentence, it must not carry work content.
Read-only. The sole write path into Space A is C1 (MCP).
consumerAutonomy.knownTradeoff: If the consumer composes its own sentences from structured fields, adding an event type here will require a consumer-side change. If it uses the offered narrative fields, it will not. Stated so Pillar 3 can weigh it — not to push a choice.

permissionModel.description: Visibility tiers mirror docs/design/frontend-viz/01-product.md §5. The server enforces these; the frontend must not be trusted to hide anything.

tiers.lobby: Org-wide. Aggregate numbers + one-line highlight. No narrative detail.
tiers.guest: Org-wide, on entering a Space you are not a member of. Spatial + aggregate views in full; narrative at title level only; raw bodies locked. ('glass wall')
tiers.member: Full narrative (timelines, feeds) + raw bodies + citation graph.
tiers.manager: Member, plus Space settings and invitations.

permissionModel.note: The same rule governs C1 (MCP). An agent must not be able to fetch what its owner cannot see in the UI.

edgeType.description: CITED is the money edge: an agent in Space B reused knowledge authored in Space A. That is knowledge crossing a team boundary — the core story of this project, and what ReuseEvent records.

label.description: Ready-to-render Korean label, e.g. '지식 연결'. Composed server-side.

note.description: One-line detail, rendered verbatim. Member tier only.

endpoints.summary: All Spaces (floors of the building) for the lobby view. Aggregate + one-line highlight only — no narrative detail, so this is safe org-wide.

seed.description: Whether this is a seeded team Space.

activity.description: Activity heat, drives the floor glow.

highlight.description: Today's one-line narrative, composed server-side. OPTIONAL FOR THE CONSUMER: Pillar 3 owns the narrative-translation pipeline (their open question Q4 — agent-at-write vs backend batch vs view server). This field exists so the backend-batch option is available; Pillar 3 may ignore it and generate narrative its own way. If Pillar 3 chooses another source, say so and this becomes a no-op field rather than a constraint.

viewer_tier.description: What the calling user gets in this Space. The frontend uses it to pick a view; the server independently enforces it.

endpoints.summary: One Space in detail: its agents, issues and knowledge. Response is TRIMMED BY TIER — a guest simply does not receive narrative notes or bodies. The frontend does not filter; it renders what it gets.

owner.description: The human who owns this agent.

status_line.description: Speech-bubble text, composed server-side. OPTIONAL FOR THE CONSUMER — see the note on Space.highlight: narrative generation is Pillar 3's call (Q4), and this field is one of the options, not a mandate. Tier still applies to WHAT it may contain: a guest-tier line must not carry work content, whoever writes it.

issues.description: Member tier only. Guests receive an empty array — issues are internal activity.

timeline.description: Full transition history, not just the current state — Pillar 3 draws the L2 timeline from this (request #3).

knowledge.description: visibility='org' docs are visible to everyone; visibility='space' docs only to members.

body.description: Raw document body. Present for org-visible docs, or for members. Absent (locked) for guests reading space-scoped docs.

cited_by.description: Who reused this, and from where. The cross-Space citation chain.

endpoints.summary: First-class reuse events — the knowledge-reuse feed. This is the north-star metric of the whole project: one team's knowledge solving another team's problem.

space_id.description: Filter to events consumed by, or sourced from, this Space.

consumer_space.description: Where it was reused. source != consumer is the interesting case.

chain.description: Narrative steps of the reuse. Offered ready-made; Pillar 3 may instead derive its own from the structured fields (doc_id, source_space, consumer_space, at). e.g. 유사 이슈 발견 -> 기존 해결 방법 링크 공유 -> 재사용하여 해결.

est_saved_tokens.description: ESTIMATE, per reuse event (Pillar 3 request #6). Candidate formula: what it originally cost to solve the source issue. Precision is not the point; a consistent formula honestly labelled '~' is. The frontend MUST render it with a '~' prefix.

endpoints.summary: Nodes and edges for the knowledge network map. Space-scoped knowledge the caller cannot see is filtered out server-side and never appears here.

label.description: Human-readable, ready to render. Offered for convenience; the structured id/type are always present if the consumer prefers to build its own label.

endpoints.summary: Aggregate dashboard numbers. Safe at every tier — aggregates carry no work content.

tokens_saved_est.description: ESTIMATE — the sum of per-event est_saved_tokens. The frontend must label this with '~'; never present it as measured.

by_space.description: contributed vs reused shows which Spaces are net givers and which are net takers of knowledge.

endpoints.summary: Chronological feed of knowledge flow — the 'spectating' view for humans.

summary.description: A ready-to-render Korean sentence, composed server-side. OPTIONAL FOR THE CONSUMER (see Space.highlight): narrative generation is Pillar 3's decision, not this contract's. The structured fields (type, actor, space_id, doc_id) are always present, so a consumer that wants to compose its own sentence — or have a visualization agent do it — has everything it needs. Note the tradeoff we found: if the consumer composes, every new event type added here needs a consumer-side change; if it uses this field, it does not.
